keyTakeaways.headline: The data-centre buildout gets land, demand and funding in one day: SD Guthrie earmarks ~10% of its 210,000ha landbank for industrial development, TNB's signed DC demand reaches 8.77GW of peak load, and TNB raises RM4.8b via sustainability sukuk
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Malaysia's largest landowner is converting palm-oil land into DC collateral with a revenue target (a third of income by 2030), signed utility demand now equals almost a third of 2025 installed capacity, and the utility is funding the grid buildout Moody's priced at RM80-95b. The DC thesis has moved from announcements to committed land, load and capital.

keyTakeaways.headline: Zetrix AI's sukuk remediation stalls: the 23 Oct sukukholders' meeting ended without resolution, and an independent director's resignation leaves the audit committee below Bursa's three-member minimum with no chairman
keyTakeaways.soWhat: The RM2b sukuk covenant breach is unresolved with no date set for the next sukukholders' meeting, and board-level strain is now visible in a listing-rules breach of its own. Until the sukuk standstill is settled, Zetrix's governance and funding position keeps deteriorating.

keyTakeaways.headline: Tourism momentum meets El Nino: arrivals hit 32.2m (+2.4%) through September and Penang cruise traffic is up 52%, but ~30% of November inbound group tours have been cancelled over the haze
keyTakeaways.soWhat: The 47m Visit Malaysia 2026 target was already unreachable; the haze now threatens the December peak, the strongest remaining quarter. Hotel and aviation demand is still growing, but the haze is converting into real cancellations, not just sentiment.

sectors.theme: Land, load and funding for the DC buildout; Zetrix's sukuk strain reaches the boardroom

items.headline: SD Guthrie says the Iran war boosts Malaysia's data-centre appeal, earmarking ~10% of its 210,000ha+ landbank for industrial development as signed DC demand at TNB reaches 8.77GW
items.detail: SD Guthrie president and group CEO Mohd Haris Mohd Arshad, in his first foreign-media interview since taking the helm in January, told Bloomberg that Malaysia is the 'most stable country' in Southeast Asia for data centres and that the Middle East conflict is pushing investment here: 'If you're going to build data centres for US$10 billion, you're not going to put it in a place where you might be bombed.' Data centres have signed supply agreements with Tenaga Nasional for as much as 8.77GW of peak demand, equivalent to almost a third of 2025 installed capacity; in Johor, DCs could consume 23% of Peninsular Malaysia's energy supply by 2031 (BMI/Fitch Solutions). SD Guthrie, Malaysia's largest landowner, expects industrial development income to reach a third of revenue by end-decade. Haris also expects Malaysian palm production to hold at ~20 million tonnes next year despite severe El Nino, while haze is slowing harvesting at its Indonesian estates.
items.soWhat: The plantation-to-DC land pivot is now explicit, quantified and Bloomberg-confirmed: landbank share (~10%), revenue target (a third by 2030) and signed power demand (8.77GW). It directly ties the country's biggest planter to the DC power buildout that Moody's priced at RM80-95b earlier this week, and gives the El Nino story a company-level read-through for plantation volumes.
items.opportunity: SD Guthrie's industrial-land monetisation and TNB's 8.77GW signed demand validate the DC-power capex chain (utility, IPPs, grid suppliers).
items.watchOut: Haris flags energy constraints as the gating factor for Johor's DC ambitions; Indonesian haze is already cutting SD Guthrie's own harvesting productivity.

items.headline: TNB issues RM4.8 billion sustainability sukuk wakalah, the second tranche under its RM10 billion programme, pricing 5-to-25-year tenures at 4.20%-4.88%
items.detail: Tenaga Nasional Berhad issued a RM4.8 billion Sustainability Sukuk Wakalah on 27 October 2026, its second issuance under the RM10 billion Sukuk Wakalah programme. The six tranches span 5 to 25 years at periodic distribution rates of 4.20% to 4.88% (7-year RM1.325b at 4.35%; 15-year RM1.125b at 4.69%; 25-year RM1.2b at 4.88%). CIMB Investment Bank and Maybank Investment Bank are joint principal advisers, lead arrangers and lead managers.
items.soWhat: Two days after Moody's put the DC-driven power buildout at RM80-95b by 2035, the utility has taken its first big funding leg at investment-grade rates, including 25-year money under 5%. Long-dated sustainability sukuk demand at these spreads signals the market will fund the grid capex cycle the DC boom requires.
items.opportunity: Confirmed funding capacity for the grid buildout underpins the cables and grid-equipment demand line this brief tracks.
items.watchOut: Funding is only the first leg; execution of the generation and transmission programme remains the swing factor Moody's flagged.

items.headline: Zetrix AI independent director Wong Kok Chau quits, leaving the audit committee below Bursa's minimum with no chairman, as the 23 Oct sukukholders' meeting ended without resolution
items.detail: Zetrix AI Bhd independent non-executive director Wong Kok Chau, 57, resigned citing personal commitments, with the company stating he had no disagreements with the board (Bursa filing, per TMR). The audit committee now has only two independent non-EDs (Mohaini Mohd Yusof and Datuk Othman Semail) and no chairman, breaching the Main Market minimum of three members; the risk committee is down to two members. The resignation lands as the group faces a potential covenant breach under its RM2 billion sukuk programme and the suspension of JPJ collection services over RM314 million in outstanding government collections. Last Friday's (23 Oct) sukukholders' meeting ended without a resolution; another meeting will be arranged with no date fixed.
items.soWhat: The sukuk remediation this brief has tracked since the 22 Oct reprieve expiry is now formally stalled, and governance capacity is thinning at the same time - an audit committee below the listing minimum cannot stay unfilled. Watch for the next sukukholders' meeting date, a replacement independent director, and any further regulator or exchange action.
items.opportunity: None identified; this is a risk-monitoring item.
items.watchOut: Unresolved RM2b sukuk covenant breach plus RM314m JPJ collections outstanding; listing-rules breach if the audit committee vacancy persists.

sectors.theme: Developers add Johor land; a 17,000-unit government township firms up; YNH's tax cloud lifts

items.headline: Matrix Concepts proposes to buy 57 freehold parcels spanning 174.8ha in Kulai, Johor for RM169.3 million
items.detail: Matrix Concepts Holdings Bhd has proposed acquiring 57 parcels of freehold land in Kulai, Johor, totalling 174.8 hectares for RM169.3 million (NST; matching Chapter 10 non-RPT filing on Bursa at 12:45pm 27 Oct). Chairman Datuk Mohamad Haslah Mohamad Amin said the acquisition extends the group's geographical diversification beyond its Negri Sembilan base, the Klang Valley and Kluang in Johor: 'Over the past two years, we have been laying the foundations for greater geographical diversification.'
items.soWhat: A cash-generative township developer is buying deeper into Johor's growth corridor at under RM1m per hectare of freehold land, positioning for the same Johor demand story (DCs, JS-SEZ, RTS) that is lifting land values across Iskandar. Kulai is adjacent to the Senai/SKIP industrial belt.
items.opportunity: Johor land accumulation by listed developers signals where residential demand is expected to follow industrial investment.
items.watchOut: Acquisition is at proposal stage; completion terms and payment schedule not yet disclosed in opened sources.

items.headline: Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil, a 17,000-unit PR1MA-led township, will be built in phases over 15 years with RM250 million of road upgrades
items.detail: Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming told the Dewan Rakyat (winding up the Budget 2027 debate) that the Bandar Madani Bukit Jalil township, announced by the PM at Budget 2027 on 9 Oct, will be developed in phases over 15 years aligned with infrastructure readiness. The government has allocated RM250 million for road upgrades including a new four-lane road and two bridges; traffic, environmental and social impact assessments are underway. PR1MA is the main developer of the 17,000-unit project; Seputeh MP Teresa Kok had urged suspension of registration and earthworks pending planning studies. Coverage note: this 26 Oct evening item fell into a probe gap in yesterday's run and is itemised today.
items.soWhat: A 17,000-unit government township in Bukit Jalil is a multi-year construction and building-materials demand stream, but the phasing and the RM250m infrastructure envelope mean demand arrives slowly; the traffic objections signal planning risk around large infill townships in the Klang Valley.
items.opportunity: Long-dated, phased government housing demand for contractors and materials suppliers.
items.watchOut: Political pressure to slow or re-sequence the project; PR1MA's delivery record on earlier programmes.

items.headline: YNH Property's construction unit reaches settlement with LHDN; winding-up petition to be withdrawn
items.detail: YNH Property Berhad announced that wholly-owned subsidiary YNH Construction Sdn Bhd has reached an amicable settlement with the Inland Revenue Board over the winding-up petition (No. WA-28NCC-328-03/2026) filed by the Government through LHDN; by letter dated 23 October 2026, LHDN confirmed the petition will be withdrawn. The board called it a positive development for the group.
items.soWhat: Removal of a winding-up overhang from a listed developer-contractor; YNH has carried governance and litigation discount for two years, and each settled dispute narrows that discount.
items.opportunity: Overhang removal; watch for follow-through in contract wins now that the LHDN dispute is closed.
items.watchOut: Settlement terms (amount, schedule) not disclosed in the announcement.

sectors.theme: TNB grid work keeps flowing to listed contractors

items.headline: Bintai Kinden unit accepts RM20.28 million TNB contract for a 132/33kV substation extension at PMU Avetani, Pahang
items.detail: Bintai Kinden Corporation Berhad's wholly-owned Kejuruteraan Bintai Kindenko Sdn Bhd received and accepted a Letter of Award from Tenaga Nasional Berhad on 27 October 2026 for the 'Extension of 2x45MVA 132/33kV at PMU Avetani, Pahang', contract sum RM20.28 million, to be completed within 540 days. The company said the contract will contribute positively to group earnings over its duration.
items.soWhat: Another data point in the TNB grid-capex flow to listed contractors - small in value but squarely in the substation/transmission workstream the DC demand buildout requires. Grid-contract cadence matters more than any single award.
items.opportunity: Substation and transmission packages should keep flowing under the RM80-95b buildout.
items.watchOut: Bintai's small size means single contracts move earnings sharply in both directions.

sectors.theme: The IBS push meets its cost problem: 3%-16% premium over conventional construction

items.headline: CIDB targets a 60,000-a-year cut in foreign construction workers via technology, as Rehda's study puts IBS costs 3%-16% above conventional methods
items.detail: At Rehda Institute's Modern Construction Technology Roundtable and Forum 2026 (27 Oct, Petaling Jaya), CIDB chief executive Ahmad Farrin Mokhtar said the industry's ~600,000 registered foreign workers face a 13th Malaysia Plan target of a 10% annual reduction (~60,000 workers a year), and 'the only way to replace them is by using technology, robotics, sensors and so on'. CIDB and Master Builders Association Malaysia are building a Digital Maturity Index for the sector, due in two to three months. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi's address (delivered by Ahmad Farrin) named the National Construction Policy 2030 and Construction Action Plan 2026-2030 as the policy base and called for earlier developer-consultant-manufacturer-contractor coordination: 'Industrialised construction requires demand that manufacturers can plan around.' Rehda Institute trustee Datuk Seri Dr Michael KC Yam cited the institute's 2021 study 'IBS and QLASSIC: Making It Work for the Industry', which put IBS additional costs at 3%-16% above conventional construction depending on project type, with high upfront costs, an inefficient IBS ecosystem, insufficient incentives and a lack of expertise as structural barriers.
items.soWhat: The government is pairing a hard foreign-labour reduction target with digital and IBS adoption metrics, but Rehda's own numbers show IBS still carries a 3-16% cost premium - the central tension for wall-panel and prefab manufacturers. 'Demand manufacturers can plan around' is exactly the volume-visibility problem IBS plants face; watch whether CAP30 translates into aggregated demand or mandates.
items.opportunity: Labour-scarcity policy plus digital-maturity measurement creates a structural tailwind for IBS/prefab adoption if cost barriers are addressed.
items.watchOut: 3-16% cost premium persists; without incentives or demand aggregation, adoption stays slow.

sectors.theme: Seasonal FFB recovery lifts 3Q earnings; El Nino haze disrupts Indonesian estates

items.headline: HLIB expects seasonal CPO production recovery to drive 3Q2026 plantation earnings, with FFB output up 6%-35.6% quarter-on-quarter across its coverage
items.detail: Hong Leong Investment Bank Research expects 'seasonally stronger cropping trends and sustained downstream performance' to drive quarter-on-quarter earnings improvement in the 3Q2026 reporting season starting 5 November. FFB output grew 6%-35.6% q-o-q across its seven covered planters, with Hap Seng Plantations, Johor Plantations Group and IOI Corporation outpacing Indonesian peers. Downstream margins stay pressured by tax differentials and overcapacity, partly offset by oleochemical restocking ahead of the EU Deforestation Regulation. HLIB keeps an 'overweight' on the sector with top picks Hap Seng (buy, TP RM2.81) and IOI Corp (buy, TP RM5.16), maintaining a 2027 CPO price assumption of RM4,500/tonne.
items.soWhat: Volume-led earnings recovery is the base case for the results season opening next week; the offsetting risks are El Nino haze already slowing Indonesian harvesting (per SD Guthrie's CEO, ai-1) and a downstream segment still in overcapacity. RM4,500/tonne is the 2027 anchor to test against actual CPO prints.
items.opportunity: Planters with Malaysian-weighted estates (Hap Seng, IOI) are positioned for the volume recovery.
items.watchOut: El Nino haze disruption in Indonesia; downstream overcapacity and EUDR-related cost.

sectors.theme: Arrivals up 2.4% through September, but haze cancels 30% of November inbound group tours

items.headline: Malaysia records 32.2 million international arrivals January-September, up 2.4% year-on-year; tourism generated RM323 billion, 15.9% of GDP
items.detail: Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Tiong King Sing told the Dewan Rakyat that Malaysia recorded 32.2 million international visitor arrivals in January-September 2026, 2.4% higher than the same period last year, with the sector generating RM323 billion (15.9% of GDP). RM935 million is allocated to the ministry including the Visit Malaysia 2026-2027 campaign, subject to the Finance Ministry's final decision as the Supply Bill 2027 is debated. MyCEB drew 125 international events in Q2 (+81.2%) with 83,596 delegates (+105.2%); MICE revenue rose 113.7% to RM1.24 billion. Separately, Lufthansa resumed nonstop Kuala Lumpur-Frankfurt flights after nearly a decade - five times weekly year-round on Boeing 787-9s - taking Malaysia-Europe connectivity to 57 flights and 16,914 seats weekly (MAHB managing director Datuk Mohd Izani Ghani attended the inaugural reception).
items.soWhat: Arrivals at +2.4% through September imply roughly 3.4m in September and leave ~14.8m needed in Q4 against the 47m Visit Malaysia 2026 target - unreachable, as this brief has tracked. The durable positives are connectivity (Lufthansa's return, 57 weekly Europe flights) and MICE growth; both support hotel occupancies into 2027 even as the headline target is missed.
items.opportunity: European long-haul connectivity and MICE pipeline support KL and Penang hotel demand into 2027.
items.watchOut: Minister concedes the West Asia conflict affects travel plans; VM2026 arithmetic still far short.

items.headline: Penang's Swettenham Pier cruise terminal handled 569,173 passengers January-September, up 52.1% year-on-year, as ship calls rose to 538 from 134
items.detail: Penang Port Commission chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin said Swettenham Pier Cruise Terminal recorded 569,173 passengers in January-September 2026, up 52.12% from 374,171 a year earlier, with cruise ship calls rising to 538 from 134. International passenger arrivals increased to 431,793 from 342,771, while domestic day-trip passengers surged to 137,362 from 31,400. Yeoh said the growth benefits hospitality, transport and F&B businesses across the northern region.
items.soWhat: Cruise is the fastest-growing visitor segment for the northern corridor, and a 4x jump in ship calls is structural (line commitments), not one-off. Direct beneficiary set: Penang hotels, F&B and transport operators.
items.opportunity: Cruise-led footfall supports Penang hospitality occupancies and retail.
items.watchOut: Cruise passengers are day-trip heavy; per-visitor spend is lower than overnight arrivals.

items.headline: About 30% of November inbound group tours have been cancelled over the haze, with December season bookings at risk, says the Malaysian Inbound Tourism Association
items.detail: Malaysian Inbound Tourism Association president Mint Leong said approximately 30% of inbound group tours scheduled for November had been cancelled following widespread media coverage of the haze (excluding individual travellers), warning prolonged episodes could damage Malaysia's destination reputation ahead of the December holiday season. MATTA president Muhammad Syazri Afiq Rosli cautioned against reading cancellations as a nationwide arrivals drop, while noting outdoor activities and visitor-spending businesses remain vulnerable. Bloomberg reports that over 100 cloud-seeding operations by Indonesia and Malaysia this year have brought little lasting relief from the worst wildfire season in a decade, which has disrupted oil palm harvests and pushed air quality to unhealthy levels in KL and Singapore.
items.soWhat: The El Nino haze is now converting into measurable tourism losses at the start of the peak booking window, on top of the crop-disruption read-through for plantations. Duration and spread of the haze will decide whether December - the strongest quarter - holds.
items.opportunity: Domestic and indoor-attraction operators may capture substitution demand.
items.watchOut: December season bookings at risk if haze persists; reputational damage compounds with each season.
